standard_prerequisites.name: Initial segments and ordinal membership
standard_prerequisites.use: At line 832: transporting the isomorphism of A_{a1} along f identifies it with the B-segment at f(a1).

standard_prerequisites.name: No well-order is isomorphic to its proper initial segment
standard_prerequisites.use: At line 835: two isomorphic B-segments must sit over the same point, forcing b1 = f(a1).

core_obligations: Direction and setup (proof lines 828-831): prove left to right, fix isomorphisms of the two segment pairs, and let f witness the larger segment A_{a2} isomorphic to B_{b2}.
Transport (lines 832-834): from a1 < a2, the sub-segment A_{a1} corresponds under f to B_{f(a1)} via the initial-segment lemma.
Rigidity close (lines 834-836): B_{b1} is isomorphic to A_{a1} isomorphic to B_{f(a1)}, so b1 = f(a1) by the non-self-embeddability lemma, and b1 lessdot b2 since b1 lies in the domain-bound B_{b2}.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to one direction by symmetry.
Push the smaller A-segment forward along the isomorphism from the larger one.
Identify the image as the B-segment over f(a1).
Use segment rigidity to pin b1 = f(a1) and conclude.
difficulty_reason: Short coherence lemma (statement 820-827 with nested display, proof 828-840): two named lemmas of the unit chained through one transport argument; the symmetric direction is a one-line remark. H2: brief but requires tracking segment notation.
